description: Correlation between the share of chromatic (non white/black/grey/silver) cars since the 1970s and Swiss interest rates. Requested as a rough estimate. Car color data exist only for the US and global markets and are used as a proxy for Switzerland. The strong positive correlation of the levels (both series fall over time) is a textbook spurious correlation: the correlation of first differences is much weaker. Version 0.0.2 adds the Momo hypothesis raised in the dialogue: Michael Ende's novel Momo (1973) was inspired by Silvio Gesell's demurrage money (Freigeld); the grey men steal time; stolen time, low interest rates and depression are linked; depressed people prefer grey. Each link is filed as a separate assumed value with its own confidence so the weakest link can be identified. An alternative mechanism (cheap leasing under low interest favours resale-safe grey colors) is filed alongside. The dialogue also noted that Gesell's Freigeld is negative interest, so the identification of demurrage money with high interest is inverted in sign. Version 0.0.3 adds the reversed-causality hypothesis from the dialogue: mood is the common cause; cheerful people spend, spending raises inflation, the central bank raises rates; depressed people prefer grey. The dialogue objects that this feedback loop explains cycles but not the fifty-year trend of both series, and proposes a direct test with the SECO consumer sentiment index. Version 0.0.4 folds the leasing hypothesis into the mood hypothesis (optimistic buyers ignore resale value), marks the resale advantage of grey as a belief rather than a measured fact, files the 1970s oil shocks as politically triggered with prior oil demand as a necessary condition, and adds two falsifiable predictions. Version 0.0.5 adds the scenario in which the grey men succeed: time is hoarded and frozen in the time savings bank. Two readings of the interest rate consequence are filed: Gesell's basic interest floor (hoarding keeps interest high) and the Keynesian savings glut reading (hoarding drives interest to zero or below), with the Swiss negative rate period 2015 to 2021 as evidence against the floor.

words.name: Keynesian reading of grey men success
words.description: reading: success of the grey men equals a savings glut, demand collapse and an interest rate at or below zero. When the grey men win, people save time, but the saved time never returns to them: it lies frozen in the vault of the time savings bank. Read economically this is hoarding without return flow. Everyone works faster and sets more aside, but nobody spends, nobody invests in what Ende calls life. Where demand is missing, prices and investment fall, and with them the interest rate, down to zero or below. The low interest rate is then not the cause of the grey time but its thermometer: it shows how much time and money lies in the vault instead of circulating. And the people who lack time turn grey like the men who took it from them. So do their cars.
